rationales: Metallic bonding occurs between metal atoms, not because of an electronegativity difference below 1.7.
An electronegativity difference below 1.7 generally indicates covalent rather than ionic bonding.
A difference below 1.7 generally indicates a covalent bond.
A coordinate covalent bond is classified by how the shared pair is donated, not by this electronegativity threshold.
Each oxygen atom shares two electron pairs with the other, forming a double covalent bond.
A single bond has only one shared electron pair, but O₂ has two.
A triple bond has three shared electron pairs, but O₂ has two.
O₂ consists of two nonmetal atoms joined by covalent bonding, not ionic bonding.
Graphite is a soft form of carbon, not an extremely hard one.
Iodine is a brittle solid, but it is not extremely hard.
Diamond is an extremely hard nonmetallic form of carbon.
Phosphorus is not an extremely hard nonmetal.
9.8 g is not the molar mass of H₂SO₄.
98 amu is the approximate molecular mass, not the molar mass expressed in grams per mole.
H₂SO₄ has a molar mass of 98 g/mol, commonly written as 98 g in this option.
9.8 amu is far below the molecular mass of H₂SO₄.
The p-subshell does not have one orbital.
The p-subshell has three orbitals, not two.
The p-subshell contains three orbitals.
Four orbitals are found in a d-subshell, not a p-subshell.
The second and third periods each contain eight elements and are called short periods.
Long periods contain more elements than the second and third periods.
“Normal periods” is not the name for the second and third periods.
Very long periods refer to the sixth and seventh periods, not the second and third.
C₂H₂ has more than two shared electron pairs.
Counting the triple bond as one bond gives three connections, but not the number of shared pairs asked for in this convention.
Four shared pairs would not account for all the bonding in H–C≡C–H.
The two C–H single bonds and the C≡C triple bond contain five shared electron pairs in total.
N₂ is nonpolar, so this pair does not both have polar covalent bonds.
O₂ and Cl₂ are homonuclear molecules and have nonpolar covalent bonds.
H₂O is polar, but C₂H₂ is generally nonpolar.
Both H₂O and HCl have polar covalent bonds.
% v/v expresses the volume of solute per volume of solution.
Mass of solute divided by mass of solution gives % m/m.
% m/v uses solute mass and solution volume, not solution mass.
% v/m expresses solute volume per solution mass.
Sugar dissolves in water.
Alcohol, such as ethanol, is soluble in water.
Glucose dissolves in water.
Benzene is nonpolar and is not soluble in water.
Avogadro’s number is approximately 6.02 × 10²³ particles, not 10²⁴.
A negative exponent gives a very small number, not Avogadro’s number.
Avogadro’s number is approximately 6.02 × 10²³ particles per mole.
6.02 × 10²⁰ is three orders of magnitude too small.
The sixth period contains more than 2 elements.
The sixth period contains more than 8 elements.
The sixth period contains more than 18 elements.
The sixth period contains 32 elements.

The N shell has principal quantum number 4 and contains four subshells.
The L shell has two subshells.
The O shell has five subshells, not four.

HCl has only two atoms and is diatomic.
H₂O has three atoms and is a polyatomic molecule.
CH₄ has five atoms and is a polyatomic molecule.

Cl₂ has identical atoms and no permanent dipole, so it is nonpolar.
HCl has a polar bond and is a polar molecule.
HF has a polar bond and is a polar molecule.
